title: Pricing Desk Rules: Monthly Variable Rates on Small Business Electricity Supply Agreements
content:
**Rule 1.** A Small Business Electricity Supply month-to-month agreement is billed at its contract rate for its first introductory rate cycles and for any cycles held at the expiring rate under the business rollover rules.

**Rule 2.** After that, each cycle is billed at the new rate of the latest variable rate change notice on the agreement whose effective date is on or before the cycle's first day; until the first such notice applies, the contract rate continues.

**Rule 3.** A business variable rate change notice must be issued at least the plan's variable rate notice days (7 calendar days on every plan) before its stated effective date; when it is issued later, the change applies only from the first cycle beginning on or after the notice date plus the variable rate notice days.

**Rule 4.** Variable rate changes never apply to a fixed plan during its term.

## Rate for a cycle of a month-to-month agreement

| Cycle | Rate billed |
|---|---|
| One of the plan's introductory rate cycles | contract rate |
| A cycle held at the expiring rate under the rollover rules | contract rate |
| Any other cycle, once a variable rate change notice applies | the new rate of the latest notice whose effective date is on or before the cycle's first day |
| Any other cycle, before any such notice applies | contract rate |

## Notice timing, worked on hypothetical dates

The agreement's cycles begin on the 3rd of each month.

| Notice date | Stated effective date | Days of notice | First cycle at the new rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 May | 1 June | 12, at least 7 | the cycle beginning 3 June |
| 28 May | 1 June | 4, fewer than 7 | the first cycle beginning on or after 4 June (28 May plus 7 days), that is the cycle beginning 3 July |

## Fixed plans

A variable rate change notice has no effect on a fixed plan during its term; the fixed plan's cycles keep the contract rate.
